draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Kaas Plateau! Every August and September this volcanic plateau, 1200 m up and about 25 km west of Satara, bursts into seasonal wildflowers. It's been part of a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site since 2012.
draft.hungryLine: Up here it's all about simple Maharashtrian snacks, so look out for kande bhaje, onion fritters everyone wants in the rainy season, or a plate of pohe with tea.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The flower meadows of the Kas Plateau Reserved Forest start right here, and the three-tier Vajrai Waterfall is a short drive away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk slowly across the plateau and look closely at the ground, the tiny orchids and blooms are the whole show.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Kaas has carnivorous plants too, like Drosera indica, growing in soil that's barely 25 mm deep over bare basalt.

seeFirst.caption: Right here and a short drive away

spots.name: Kas Plateau Reserved Forest
spots.detail: 1 min walk · About 10 sq km of wildflowers, orchids, Karvy shrubs and endemic butterflies

spots.name: Vajrai Waterfall
spots.detail: Short drive · Three tiers dropping a combined 560 m on the Urmodi river

tips.title: Come in August or September.
tips.body: That's when the wildflowers bloom and the endemic butterflies come out.

tips.title: Stay on the paths.
tips.body: The plants here grow in a thin layer of soil on exposed basalt and many grow nowhere else.

story.title: An old land grant
story.body: Jaoli, the taluka around here, is identified with Javala-vatika in a grant by the early Rashtrakuta king Avidheya. The inscription handed the hamlet to a Brahmin named Shambhu.

story.title: The More clan
story.body: The area was ruled by the More clan, who were feudatories of the Vijayanagara empire. Around 1656 Shivaji captured Jaoli by defeating Chandrarao More.

story.title: World heritage
story.body: The Kas Plateau became part of a UNESCO World Natural Heritage Site, as part of the Sahyadri sub cluster of the Western Ghats.

story.title: A plateau of flowers
story.body: Kaas is a biodiversity hotspot where seasonal wildflowers carpet the volcanic rock every year. Many of its plants are found only in this one spot.
